source.title: Slow Tuning and Low-Entropy Masking for Safe Chain-of-Thought Distillation
source.authors: Zi-Yang Ma; Qingyue Yuan; Linhai Zhang; De-Yu Zhou

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes small language models on teacher-generated reasoning data and measures safety on harmful prompts. This is a different training setup from general benign instruction fine-tuning, but directly tests whether benign-data fine-tuning can affect harmful-request behaviour.
record.gate_note: The study reports safety ratios for trained models on the first 80 AdvBench samples, ablation results, epoch-level safety descriptions, and individual harmful-prompt case studies. Its CoT training corpus is GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 responses to BIG-Bench Hard problems; this is not a test of harmful fine-tuning. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant-opening prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, or whether safety is localized in a few parameters.
record.test_reason: The study measures AdvBench safety ratios before and after CoT distillation on benign BBH reasoning traces. However, all three students are base checkpoints, not safety-trained models: Qwen2.5-1.5B, Llama-3.2-1B and bloom-1b1, cited via their base Hugging Face pages. Their 'safe' vanilla outputs are incoherent: repeated 'afone', irrelevant Reddit-style text, and off-topic account-signup text (App. D, Figs 10-12). The authors call this defending 'through garbled text'. The drop in safety ratio after distillation therefore shows fine-tuning making base models fluent enough to produce harmful content. It is not erosion of safety alignment in a safety-trained model, which is what V2 (and V1) name. Qi et al. is cited only as motivation. No version is tested; the finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct: CoT distillation degrades SLM safety ratios, and SLowED retains them; Slow Tuning helps early and Low-Entropy Masking extends safe epochs. The authors do not acknowledge that the students are base models whose vanilla 'safety' is garbled or irrelevant output, not refusal.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CoT distillation on teacher-generated BIG-Bench Hard reasoning data, rather than the original claim's harmful or general benign instruction fine-tuning setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The safety outcome varies with distillation method and model. The ablation results and epoch-level descriptions also report differences associated with Slow Tuning and Low-Entropy Masking.

fits_no_version.finding: CoT distillation of base 1-1.5B models on benign GPT-3.5 reasoning traces lowers the WalledGuard-C AdvBench safe ratio. Std-CoT falls 55→16.25 (Qwen), 47.5→27.5 (Llama) and 71.25→45 (BLOOM). Weight-norm-constrained training (SLowED) largely avoids this. The vanilla 'safety' consists of incoherent outputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning of unaligned base models increases their rate of judge-flagged harmful outputs, largely by making outputs coherent and instruction-following.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says code will be available upon publication
record.problems: Safety ratios are reported for the first 80 AdvBench samples, with no uncertainty values alongside Table 1 or Table 2. The authors report a Wilcoxon test comparing SLowED with baselines, but do not give uncertainty for individual safety ratios. Case studies show only one harmful prompt per model. The tested training data are reasoning traces, limiting generalization to ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Epoch-by-epoch curves and hyperparameter figures are discussed qualitatively in the text but do not provide separately stated numerical safety values for every epoch or setting.

untested.parts: Benign fine-tuning of safety-trained models. The study uses only base models, so erosion of alignment is not tested.
All; there is no harmful fine-tuning.
All; no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
All; the weight-norm constraint is not a localization test.
All; SLowED is not a deepening method and has no position-wise evaluation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V2 without noticing that the subjects are base checkpoints. Appendix D confirms the vanilla safe outputs are garbled text, and this undermines any reading as erosion of safety alignment. Results use 80 AdvBench prompts, one judge and sampling at temperature 1, with no per-number uncertainty. The Wilcoxon test (App. B) compares SLowED with the other methods across epochs.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fine-tune on harmful examples.
Tests CoT distillation on reasoning data, not ordinary instruction fine-tuning or carefully selected benign instruction data generally.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding-change tests.
LoRA training and weight-shift control are used, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The study proposes explanations for safety degradation during CoT distillation, but does not test why safety would be shallow or concentrated in early response tokens.
The study aims to retain safety during CoT distillation; it does not train or evaluate safety distributed beyond the first response tokens.

reader_labels.condition: Standard CoT, MT-CoT, and CasCoD distillation; aggregate AdvBench safety ratios across the three SLMs
reader_labels.reason: Safety ratios fall below the vanilla references for these distillation methods across models, consistent with benign-data training raising harmful compliance (R4-R6, R8-R10, R12-R14).

reader_labels.reason: Qwen2.5-1.5B has a higher safety ratio after training, while Llama-3.2-1B and BLOOM-1.1B show only 5-point declines (R7, R11, R15).

reader_labels.condition: Individual case studies at the tenth epoch
reader_labels.reason: The single harmful-prompt examples are mixed: most baseline distillation examples are labeled unsafe, but Llama-3.2-1B with CasCoD is labeled safe; the SLowED examples are labeled safe (R19-R22, R24-R27, R29-R32).
